speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: The facts and the Court's interpretation are all set out there.

speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim)
text: It can be freely accessed from the Supreme Court website.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Ms Sylvia Lim, just be careful as this matter is before the Court of Appeal.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Yes, Madam, I am aware of that and I do not intend to ask any questions concerning the merits of the case on either side, but just to clarify some chronology of events and some undisputed facts.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Originally, I filed the question with Ministry of Law.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: So, I can understand if Minister Yaacob may not be comfortable, but I have to ask the question to the Government.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Usually, these cases are over in just a few months, at most, six months.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The third question is: I understand that there is a pending application now on the evidence before the Court as to how the transcripts were taken from the Lee family house to be in the hands of the Cabinet.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The last question is: the transcripts, according to what we understand, is supposed to be kept by the Cabinet Secretary.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I suppose the Judges have to examine all the evidence.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: I think our Judiciary works very carefully to make sure that we come up with the best possible judgment.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Whether the Judge did this or not, again, I cannot comment because it is basically the prerogative of the Judiciary to decide on the best course of action.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: As to why the transcripts were read at MHA and all that, again, as I said earlier, because there is an appeal, I do not think it is appropriate for me to comment at this point.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: I understand the Minister cannot comment on the merits and I am not asking about the merits at all.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: In fact, the first question which I asked I think still merits an answer in the sense that this decision by the Judge to expunge the evidence about how the transcripts travelled from the house to the Cabinet, I am now asking whether the Government, during the case, made the request for the evidence to be suppressed or did the Judge do it on his own volition.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: I do not think that touches on the merits.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Did the Government make that request or did the Judge decide it on his own accord?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: The last question about why the transcripts were perused at MHA, I do not think that is a question for the Court to decide at all because it is just a fact that the family was asked to go to MHA to peruse the transcripts.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: So, I am just asking why was that the case?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: I am not saying that there is anything wrong; I am just asking for a clarification as to why if the transcripts have to be kept at the Cabinet Secretary, they were made available to the family at MHA.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Again, Madam, I am in no position to comment as to what were the reasons behind the various things that the Member asked.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: Clearly, I would believe that the Judiciary and the Government have given the best possible evidence in order for them to come to the best decision possible.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: As to the process by which the transcripts had been shown to the family, again, I think there must be some reason for doing so.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Yaacob Ibrahim
text: At the end of the day, I think this is something which the Government would try its very best to make sure that we can get the best solution possible.
